A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Heterogeneous Decentralized Diffusion Models. All 32 pages of each version, including the supplementary sections, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison despite substantial relocation and rewriting.

before.justification: v1 reports original LAION experiments comparing decentralized training, objective conversion, routing strategies, and homogeneous versus heterogeneous experts, with quantitative results and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally displays validation-loss trajectories for pretrained versus scratch initialization in supplementary Figure 6.

M1.justification: The reported procedure is substantially revised: block-specific 6Ld modulation becomes a shared 6d vector; the final projection is transferred instead of reinitialized; rounded timestep indices become continuous 999t scaling; and learned null embeddings become frozen CLIP empty-string embeddings. Router training also changes its stated noising convention. These explicit replacements affect architecture and training, although the PDFs do not establish whether implementations or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the 11M-image LAION-Aesthetics subset and 3.9M-image LAION-Art coverage for text-to-image generation. The added loss analysis and rearranged qualitative examples introduce no new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same comparators, including the monolithic model, prior DDM, native DDPM/FM, converted DDPM, schedule combinations, and objective mixtures. Pretrained versus scratch initialization was already compared in v1 Figure 3.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 replaces objective-dependent router timestep ranges with a common Flow Matching interpolation path, uniformly sampled over [0,1] and scaled by 999. Benchmark splits, evaluation metrics, CFG/step settings, and the 500K-step expert training budget remain unchanged. This is a reported training-protocol revision, not evidence of rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: New Section 6.5 and Figure 6 add quantitative validation-loss trajectories to the existing pretrained-versus-scratch initialization analysis. Routing-threshold, expert-ordering, noise-schedule, and sampling-strategy analyses are retained; moving the threshold sweep into the supplement does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: The CLIP uncertainty values in Table 3, intra-prompt LPIPS uncertainty reporting, and matched-seed descriptions are retained. The new loss plot introduces no reported repeated-run counts, uncertainty bands, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. Figure 6 adds loss trajectories and caption estimates of 0.030 versus 0.025 loss reduction over 5K steps. Section 6.4 replaces 72 GPU-days for experts and nine parallel days with 120 A40 GPU-days including router training and 15 parallel days, normalized to 72 A100-equivalent days. Figure 3 removes four displayed examples per condition.

T1.justification: Formal model definitions change, notably the conditioning map from a 6Ld output with block-specific slices to a shared 6d output, and the timestep map from round(999t) to 999t. Proposition 1, its proof, and the schedule-aware velocity-conversion derivations retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions remain. The quantified initialization claim changes from 1.2× convergence acceleration to 1.2× faster loss reduction. Resource claims now specify A100-equivalent compute and raise the stated minimum GPU memory from 20GB to 24GB.

C2.justification: v2 removes explicit limitations concerning fixed expert membership/router retraining and evaluation limited to text-to-image generation. Section 7.3 softens the low-noise conversion recommendation from strong empirical evidence to a qualitative suggestion. Section 7.5 also qualifies the explanation connecting small expert subsets to prior mixture-of-experts practice.

D1.justification: Section 6.2 newly specifies variance-channel truncation and modulation transfer at reference timestep 500, and reconciles its velocity-scaling description with the existing piecewise rule in Section 8.3. Resource accounting now explains A40 hardware, router inclusion, and throughput normalization. Conversely, the LLaVA recaptioning description and exact sd-vae-ft-mse checkpoint reference/link disappear. These substantially revise reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kingma and Gao's diffusion-objective analysis to explain noise-level weighting, while removing the Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes and StabilityAI checkpoint references. Positioning against DDM and single-model objective-conversion methods remains broadly unchanged; extensive condensation and relocation of related work mainly affect presentation.

P1.justification: v2 moves related work before the method, merges the heterogeneous-method subsections, substantially condenses experimental setup and comparison prose, relocates the routing-threshold discussion, and rewrites the conclusion and limitations into shorter paragraphs. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds the validation-loss plot, reduces each Figure 3 grid from 16 to 12 examples, exchanges samples between Figures 1 and 7, and moves the existing threshold plot from main Figure 4 to supplementary Figure 13. Table 2 loses its reduction-summary row and expands its compute caption. Most visual evidence and the overall design are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical transparency by reconciling conflicting velocity-scaling descriptions, specifying checkpoint transfer more precisely, and distinguishing actual A40 training time from A100-equivalent compute. Figure 6 makes the lower pretrained validation loss inspectable, although its precise 1.2× rate estimate remains weakly documented. These limited gains outweigh the loss of some preprocessing/access details and limitations discussion; the retained benchmark results provide no new performance improvement.
